Customer: provide 3 golden prompt examples and 250 sample records by 2026-03-31
action_items: Alex Reyes - Send POC runbook, pricing and dedicated capacity options - due 2026-03-30
Mei Chen - Draft baseline benchmark plan (latency, throughput, accuracy) - due 2026-04-02

summary: Discovery + POC scoping meeting focused on quality evaluation plan for a NovaHealth clinical summarization assistant. Agreed success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark metrics, golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, and a 4-week POC timeline with clear next steps.
topics: Quality eval plan: golden prompts, regression suites, hallucination detection, format checks
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - I’m Alex from Redwood, with Mei and Daniel.
[00:06] Dr. Sarah Patel (NovaHealth): Sarah here.
[00:08] Tom Brooks (NovaHealth): Tom joining.
[00:09] Lina Gomez (NovaHealth): Lina.
[00:10] Ethan Wu (NovaHealth): Ethan, security.
[00:12] Alex: Great - goal today is to align on the POC scope specifically around quality evaluation: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, scoring approach, plus workload sizing and timelines. We have about 40 minutes. Sound good?
[00:23] Dr. Sarah Patel: Yes - we really want to validate clinical summarization accuracy and reduce hallucinations. Our legal and compliance folks will need to see a clear evaluation plan.
[00:31] Mei (Redwood SE): Perfect. Can you give a quick overview of your target user flows and expected load? That helps size the benchmarks.
[00:38] Tom: Our main use case is extracting and summarizing clinician notes into a standard SOAP-like structure for downstream analytics. Initially it's batch processing of end-of-day notes and also an interactive summarization tool used by clinicians - so both high-throughput and low-latency interactive.
[00:51] Alex: Good - any SLAs you target for interactive flows? p95 latency?
[00:55] Tom: For interactive, ideally p95 under 800ms for short notes (~200 tokens). If hosted can't meet that, we can accept up to 1.5s but that will impact adoption. Batch throughput should be able to process roughly 50k notes per day for the pilot.
[01:09] Mei: Noted. For sizing, can you share average and 95th percentile token lengths?
[01:13] Dr. Sarah Patel: Average note length ~450 tokens, but summaries are typically 60-120 tokens. Heavy notes hit 2k tokens occasionally.
[01:23] Mei: Okay - for the POC we'll plan benchmarks around average 450 input/100 output tokens and a heavy tail test at 2k input tokens.
[01:31] Alex: Let's talk success criteria. From our side we usually separate infra SLOs (latency/cost) from quality SLOs (accuracy/regression). What would be a pass for NovaHealth?
[01:41] Dr. Sarah Patel: Clinically, we need: 1) <5% factual error rate on critical fields (meds, dosages, allergies), 2) Formatting adherence to template 95% of the time, 3) No PII leakage - though data is de-identified for POC, security checks still required. If those are met we can move to pilot.
[01:57] Lina: And we want the summaries to include a clearly labeled risk section when any uncertain or conflicting info is present.
[02:05] Alex: Great - so quantifiable criteria: factual error <=5% on critical fields, template format compliance >=95%, hallucination detection triggers for uncertain content. We'll encode those in the eval plan.
[02:16] Tom: Also want to see tokenized cost impact - approximate cost per 1k tokens on Redwood hosted vs dedicated. That helps procurement.
[02:23] Alex: We'll include estimates and a simple cost/latency tradeoff table.
[02:28] Mei: Moving into the quality eval plan - our recommended approach is multi-pronged: 1) Golden prompts (hand-curated set of 50-100 representative prompts), 2) Regression suite (250+ labeled examples, stratified by note type), 3) Automated checks: hallucination heuristics, format/JSON schema validation, field-level extraction scoring, 4) Human review for borderline cases and a small blind review panel for clinical acceptability.
[02:51] Dr. Sarah Patel: 50-100 golden prompts seems reasonable. We have a set of about 100 annotated examples from prior research that we can share after approvals.
[02:59] Alex: Perfect. For scoring: we typically compute a composite score. Example weights: 50% field-level accuracy (F1 for extracted entities), 20% template/format compliance (schema pass rate), 20% hallucination metric (false positive detection rate), 10% human acceptability (avg rating). If composite >= 85% it's a pass - but we can tune weights.
[03:21] Tom: That mapping makes sense; can we also get per-field thresholds? e.g., meds F1 >= 0.92, allergies recall >= 0.95?
[03:29] Mei: Yes - we'll propose per-field thresholds in the eval spreadsheet.
[03:33] Dr. Sarah Patel: How do you measure hallucinations automatically?
[03:36] Mei: A few heuristics and models: 1) entity grounding - if an extracted medication/dose doesn't match any token span in source, flag; 2) cross-check against patient record metadata (if no prior meds, raise low-confidence flag); 3) semantic embedding similarity between extracted assertion and source sentences - low similarity indicates potential hallucination. We output a hallucination score per instance and calibrate threshold with human labels.
[03:59] Alex: We'll include a hallucination threshold tuned to keep false positives low; human review will help refine.
[04:05] Tom: For format checks - we need a strict JSON schema for summary output. If output deviates, it's a failure for that instance.
[04:12] Mei: Agreed - we'll provide a schema and a tolerant/strict mode for scoring; strict is used for clinical integration.
[04:19] Dr. Sarah Patel: What about regression tests? We need to ensure model updates don't regress critical fields.
[04:23] Alex: The regression suite will be a frozen set of ~500 examples (we can start with 250 labeled + 250 synthetic edge cases). For any new model/quantization change, we run the regression and require no more than 1% degradation in composite score and zero regression on critical-field recall (meds/allergies).
[04:41] Mei: We'll also track token-level differences and a diff report highlighting changed outputs for triage.
[04:46] Ethan (Security): On data handling - PII is removed for POC, but our security team will want to see KMS integration, VPC peering options for Private deployment, and audit logs. Any plans for on-prem or VPC?
[04:57] Alex: Yes - Redwood Private supports customer VPC + KMS/HSM for keys and audit logs. For the POC we can start hosted with logs retention controls; if you need VPC it's doable but adds ~1-2 weeks for setup.
[05:10] Ethan: We likely need VPC for pilot after POC, but hosted POC first is fine if we have encryption-in-transit & at-rest, and SOC2 docs.
[05:19] Alex: We'll attach SOC2 and security whitepaper in the follow-up.
[05:23] Dr. Sarah Patel: Timeline - what are you proposing for a 4-week POC?
[05:27] Mei: Typical schedule: Week 0 (kickoff/integration): wire up API, data upload, small smoke tests. Week 1: baseline run on your 250 labeled examples and host vs dedicated throughput baseline. Week 2: tune prompts/quantization and run golden prompts + extended regression (500). Week 3: run hallucination/format suite, human review, and produce composite report. Week 4: triage/regression re-run and final handoff.
[05:50] Alex: Deliverables include the eval spreadsheet (golden prompts, per-field thresholds), benchmark results, hallucination calibration, and final pass/fail recommendation.
[06:00] Tom: For workload sizing - peak interactive concurrency is about 20 concurrent clinicians during peak hours; expected QPS 10-20 for interactive. Batch night-run ~50k notes/day -> roughly sustained throughput of 3-6 notes/sec with spikes.
[06:14] Mei: We'll provision tests at those rates; for hosted we can show scaling behavior and for dedicated we'll show latency/cost predictability.
[06:21] Alex: For benchmarks, we'll measure: mean latency, p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec throughput, cost per 1k tokens, composite quality score, per-field F1/recall.
[06:33] Dr. Sarah Patel: For human review, can we do a blind panel of 3 clinicians evaluating a random sample of 200 outputs for acceptability?
[06:41] Alex: Absolutely - we'll include that and provide an annotation UI link for reviewers.
[06:46] Lina: Also include checks for any change in phrasing that could alter clinical meaning - not just entity extraction.
[06:52] Mei: We'll have a 'semantic drift' check via embedding similarity and reviewer flags.
[06:57] Tom: Can you run tests against both Redwood tuned models and an open model baseline (to compare)?
[07:01] Alex: Yes - we'll run Redwood-curated open models + a tuned variant; we'll include an off-the-shelf baseline like GPT-style or other open checkpoint for comparison.
[07:10] Dr. Sarah Patel: Regarding scoring approach - you mentioned composite weighting. Can we see a draft with adjustable weights and an interactive dashboard?
[07:17] Alex: We'll send an eval spreadsheet with fields and formulas and a demo dashboard with per-test breakdowns.
[07:22] Mei: Important note - for any automatic pass/fail gating we'd recommend conservative thresholds to avoid false negatives; manual review handles gray areas.
[07:30] Ethan: Audit logs are critical. For hosted POC, what's retention and granularity?
[07:35] Alex: Logs include request/response IDs, model version, timestamps, and audit trail. Retention can be configured; default 30 days for POC. We'll include redaction controls for PII.
[07:45] Dr. Sarah Patel: OK. A few open questions from our side: 1) How do you calibrate hallucination thresholds? 2) What is the required effort to run private (VPC) option? 3) Can you support schema-strict output blocking when integration is in place?
[08:00] Mei: 1) We calibrate thresholds by sampling 200-400 outputs, label hallucinations, and choose threshold to achieve target false positive/negative tradeoff. 2) VPC setup: typically 5-10 engineer days + networking approvals, so estimate 1-2 weeks. 3) Yes - we can enforce schema strictness via output validators and optional fallback to a safe response.
[08:18] Alex: Let's capture explicit success criteria for the POC: (a) Composite score >=85% with no critical-field regression, (b) p95 latency <=1.0s for interactive on average input, (c) batch processing throughput to handle 50k/day within nightly window, (d) security checklist satisfied (SOC2 docs + KMS).
[08:36] Dr. Sarah Patel: We agree to those, want to lock per-field thresholds in spreadsheet.
[08:41] Tom: Procurement will need cost estimates and a recommended Dedicated vs Hosted decision tree.
[08:46] Alex: We'll include a simple decision tree and cost per 1k tokens for hosted vs example dedicated committed capacity.
[08:52] Mei: Any concerns about model drift during POC? We recommend running regression tests on each model change and freezing the baseline model used for scoring.
[08:59] Dr. Sarah Patel: Agreed.
[09:01] Alex: Alright - recap and actions: Redwood will share POC runbook + eval spreadsheet and security docs by 2026-03-30. Customer to share golden prompts (3 examples now, 100 after approvals) and 250 sample rows by 2026-03-31. Kickoff integration week of 2026-04-06.
[09:18] Dr. Sarah Patel: That works.
[09:20] Alex: Anything else?
[09:22] Tina: (laugh) No, that's a lot.
[09:24] Alex: Cool. Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc links.
[09:29] Tom: Thanks.
[09:31] Alex: End call.
